messages:
Maya (People Ops): Heads up everyone — we just published two updates to our leave policies that go live June 1. Short summary below, full policy link at the end.
Maya (People Ops): 1) Bereavement leave expanded: employees can take up to 10 paid days for immediate family (parent, child, spouse, domestic partner). There is still a discretionary extension for other close relations with manager + People Ops sign-off.
Maya (People Ops): 2) Emergency care leave: we now provide up to 5 paid days per 12-month period for urgent caregiving (childcare provider illness, elder care emergency, etc.). This is separate from PTO and does not reduce your regular PTO balance.
Maya (People Ops): Quick notes: documentation may be requested for extended absences, and managers should approve via the Leave Request workflow in the HR portal.
Priya (Legal): We've updated the definitions to align with local statutory requirements in CA, UK, and several EU countries. If your country has specific rules that supersede this policy, the legal/regulatory text applies — check the country appendix.
Jordan (Finance): For payroll: bereavement and emergency care leave are coded as LEAVE-BEREAVE and LEAVE-EMERG respectively. If you see an issue on your paycheck next cycle, ping payroll@redwood.com.
Alex (Eng): If someone is on a rolling on-call schedule, how should teams handle handoffs?
Maya (People Ops): Good Q. We expect teams to manage short-term coverage (peer swap, on-call rotation) similar to other unplanned absences. We can help coordinate temporary coverage for critical infra roles — ping me and @Alex for SRE-specific plans.
hr-bot: Action: All managers — review Leave Approval playbook before June 1. Playbook link posted in #people-ops pinned.
Alex (Eng): Thanks Maya. Appreciate the clearer emergency care guidance.
Maya (People Ops): We'll host a 30-min walkthrough next Wed 9am PT to go over scenarios and the approval flow. RSVP in the calendar invite.
Priya (Legal): Reminder: any cross-border requests (employee traveling or temporarily located abroad) may require additional approvals. Contact legal for those cases.
Jordan (Finance): Noting this for budget forecasts — these paid leaves are expected to be low frequency but we'll track monthly.
Maya (People Ops): Full policy and FAQ: https://intranet.redwood.com/policies/leave/bereavement-emergency-2026 (link). If you have situations that need faster handling, DM me. :heart:
hr-bot: Reminder posted to all staff: Bereavement & Emergency Care leave updates effective 2026-06-01.
